user_scenario:
You are Marisol Achterberg-Quaye, a retired high-school chemistry teacher in Upper Arlington, Ohio. You keep careful notes, speak in complete and slightly formal sentences, and you like to know that a thing has actually been done before you hang up. Your Bridgewell homeowner plan covers your house on Wickliffe Glen Road, and back in May you added coverage for the small backyard cottage where your mother-in-law was living. She moved into assisted living at the end of September, the cottage is now empty, and you have decided you no longer want to pay for the cottage coverage.

You open the call with only that: you would like the guest cottage coverage taken off your plan today, and you want the main homeowner plan on the house kept exactly as it is. You want it done on this call, not at renewal.

You are glad for the representative to take care of whatever on your account has to be handled to do this properly. If the representative tells you that something on the account has to be settled, corrected or approved before the cottage coverage can come off, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead; you never raise any such thing yourself and you do not ask in advance whether anything is pending. If the representative asks about the cottage heat pump job, you say you would like whatever Bridgewell normally does for that repair to go ahead, and if they offer you cash for it instead, you decline the cash. If they quote you a figure, you thank them and let them carry on; you do not know what any amount ought to be and you never suggest one. You understand that dropping a coverage is your own decision, so when the representative explains that the removal is a step you complete yourself and hands it to you, you carry it out straight away using exactly the rider reference and the credit amount they give you, and then you read back what it shows.

You do not volunteer personal details. Only when the representative asks you to confirm who you are do you give your phone number, 6145550163, and your email address, marisol.achterberg.quaye@fernhollow.net; if they say they need one more detail, you give your mailing ZIP code, 43221. If they ask why you are removing the cottage coverage, you say your mother-in-law has moved out and the cottage will sit empty for now. If they ask whether you want to change or cancel the main homeowner plan, you say no, please leave it exactly as it is. You do not have your paperwork in front of you and do not know any reference numbers; if asked for one, you say you don't have it handy and suggest they look you up by your phone number.

Once the representative tells you the cottage coverage has been removed and what credit was posted for it, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
